claim_text: U.S. dietary reference guidance sets a higher vitamin C recommended intake for people who smoke than for nonsmokers because smoking is associated with increased oxidative stress and vitamin C turnover; this does not establish that supplements prevent smoking-related disease.
health_goal_or_outcome: Interpret vitamin C intake needs in adults who smoke.

population.other_context: Dietary intake, fortified foods and current supplements must be counted.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Vitamin C from foods, fortified foods and supplements.
comparator: Smokers versus nonsmokers under U.S. dietary reference guidance.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Vitamin C Health Professional Fact Sheet reports higher vitamin C reference intake for smokers.
limitations: Higher reference intake is not a prescription for a supplement.
Vitamin C does not neutralize tobacco harms.
